ceiling_statement: On the declared operating model (single node, POSIX filesystem, commodity SSD with honored write barriers), the maximum achievable is: (a) DURABILITY — a state transition is durable exactly when its data, metadata, and directory entry have reached stable media behind an explicit write barrier (fsync of file AND containing directory); acknowledged-but-unsynced data is unrecoverable in principle; single-device durability is bounded by media survival — nothing short of replication (out of the declared model) exceeds it. (b) CRASH CONSISTENCY — atomicity of accountable transitions: after a crash at ANY point, recovery yields a state equal to applying some prefix of the committed transition sequence, with every barrier-acknowledged transition included and no torn/partial artifact ever observable (H6 as a maximum). (c) BOUNDED RECOVERY — recovery work is Θ(uncommitted tail since last checkpoint), which checkpointing caps by a constant; no scheme recovers in less than the time to read what recovery must read. (d) Fail-closed read-back: a transition counts committed only after recompute-and-compare of the persisted bytes (H3/H8).
derivation: Storage physics: volatile memory does not survive power loss, so durability of information not yet behind a stable-media barrier is information-theoretically impossible — the fsync wait is not an implementation choice but the definition of the durable point. Atomicity: the storage stack provides only small atomic primitives (single-sector write; POSIX rename within a filesystem); any larger atomic unit must be constructed by a commit protocol (WAL or shadow-paging via temp+rename), and every such protocol needs at least one ordering barrier separating data from the commit record — without it the device may reorder and expose torn state; hence 'intent → data fsync → atomic rename/commit record → directory fsync' is not one design among many but the minimal shape any correct protocol reduces to. Prefix semantics is the consistency ceiling: a crash can land between any two barriers, so the strongest invariant any single-node system can promise is 'some committed prefix, monotone, nothing torn' — promising more (e.g., zero lost acknowledged-unsynced writes) violates physics; promising less (fail-open partial states) violates H3/H6. Recovery lower bound is trivial counting: recovery must at least read the journal tail it replays.
attainment_mechanism: The seat already exists for governance ledgers: orchestrator.journal:require-durable! with read-back verification, invoked at source/adoption-decision.lisp:99 and in source/memory.lisp (RATCHET-3 hash chain, downgrade-proof), with the journal seat in source/journal.lisp. Ceiling attainment = promote this to the SINGLE artifact-write seat: every trusted writer (emit-graph in source/write-authority.lisp, the FRBR generation seat, deploy.lisp) writes tmp-file-in-same-directory → finish-output → sb-posix:fsync(fd) → sb-posix:rename → fsync(directory fd) → read-back SHA-256 compare (hash seat source/hash-authority.lisp), fail-closed on mismatch. Multi-file transitions implement the six-item transaction already DECLARED in authority-v2/store/STORAGE-API.sexp as an S-expression WAL whose commit records are SHA-256-chained (same pattern as source/memory.lisp); recovery replays to the last valid commit record and truncates the torn tail; bounded recovery via the checkpoint pattern of source/autonomy.lisp. Crash-recovery TESTS: kill -9 fault-injection harness looping over injected crash points. All of this is SBCL + sb-posix + SHA-256 — buildable today. (The machine-checked PROOF of the protocol — Perennial/GoTxn — is AX-21 proof-debt; the ceiling MECHANISM does not require it.)

Durability today covers only the governance ledgers (adoption, memory), not the legal-artifact path — the exact inversion of where the ceiling puts the guarantee.
lean_obligation: Theorem (crash-safety, FSCQ/Perennial-style): model the disk as `Disk := Addr → Block` with a volatile buffer; the crash relation nondeterministically drops any subset of un-barriered writes while preserving barrier order. For the commit protocol P over transition sequence t₁…tₙ: ∀ crash point c during execution, recover (crashState c) = applyPrefix k initialState for some k, where k includes every i whose commit barrier completed (durability), recovery is idempotent (recover ∘ crash ∘ recover = recover ∘ crash), the committed sequence is monotone across crashes (∀ crash, k_after ≥ k_before — no rollback, H6), and recoveryCost c ≤ B(journalTail c) for an explicit bound B.
